questions.question: What is the study of rocks called?
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">What is the study of rocks called?</font></font>
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Petrology.

Key Points

  • Petrology
    •  Petrology is the scientific study of rocks, encompassing their origin, composition, texture, and structure.
    • It delves into the processes that form and transform rocks, such as igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary processes.
    •  Petrologists investigate the mineral composition of rocks, their physical properties, and the geological conditions under which they formed.
    • This field plays a crucial role in understanding the Earth's history and the dynamics of geological processes.

Additional Information

  • Fruit Science (Pomology)
    • Pomology is the branch of horticulture that focuses on the cultivation, breeding, and study of fruits.
    •  It encompasses various aspects of fruit production, including tree and vine training, fruit quality assessment, disease and pest management, and the development of new fruit varieties.
    • Pomology contributes to improving fruit production, enhancing fruit quality, and ensuring sustainable fruit cultivation practices.
  • Mycology
    • Mycology is the scientific study of fungi.
    • It explores the biology, genetics, biochemistry, taxonomy, and ecology of fungi, which include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
    • Mycology has significant implications in various fields, including medicine (antibiotics, immunology), agriculture (mycorrhizae, biocontrol agents), and industry (food production, bioremediation).
  • Soil Science (Pedology)
    • Soil science is the study of soil, its formation, properties, classification, and management.
    •  It investigates soil composition (minerals, organic matter), soil structure, soil water, soil fertility, and the impact of human activities on soil quality.
    • Soil science is crucial for sustainable agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding the Earth's ecosystems.

questions.question: The ________ is the highest battle field in the world.
questions.questionHtml: The ________ is the highest battle field in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. Siachin Glacier.

Key Points

Siachin Glacier

  • The Siachen Glaciers, known as the world's highest battlefield. Hence option 4 is correct.
  • It is located in the eastern Karakoram mountain range in the Himalayas.
  • The Saltoro Ridge of the Siachin glacier serves as a divider that prevents direct linking of PoK with China, stopping them to develop geographical military linkages in the area.
  • Siachen also serves as a watchtower for India to keep a deep watch on Gilgit and Baltistan regions of Pakistan.
  • Besides the twin military threats from Pakistan and China, the climate condition is the biggest challenge for the armed forces.
  • The temperature in Siachen glacier in winters drops to below -60 degrees.
  • There are also constant threats of avalanches, crevasses on the glacier, high-speed winds.
  • Soldiers stationed in the area are affected by a range of fatal altitude-related ailments like frostbites, hypoxia, hypothermia and whiteouts etc.

questions.question: When does the entire earth experience equal days and nights?
questions.questionHtml: When does the entire earth experience equal days and nights?
questions.solution:
• On the Day of equinox, the entire earth experience equal days and nights. 
  • An equinox occurs when the plane of Earth's equator passes through the center of the Sun. It takes place twice in a year-March 21 and September 23. However, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.
  • Winter Solstice-It is the shortest period of daylight and longest night of the year. In this, the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt away from the Sun.
  • It occurs twice a year. It occurs once in Northern Hemisphere and once in Southern Hemisphere.
  • Northern Hemisphere Winter Solstice: 21st December, Southern Hemisphere Winter Solstice: 21st June. Again, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.
  • Summer Solistice-It is the longest period of daylight and shortest night of the year. In this, the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt towards the Sun. 
  • It occurs twice a year. It occurs once in Northern Hemisphere and once in Southern Hemisphere.
  • Northern Hemisphere Summer Solstice: 21st June, Southern Hemisphere Summer Solstice: 22nd December. Again, the dates can sometimes vary by a day or two because of difference in leap and non-leap years.

questions.question: Which are the two wettest places on Earth that receive more than 1,080 cm of rainfall in a year?

questions.solution: The two wettest places on Earth, receiving over 1,080 cm of rainfall annually, are Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India. questions.solution: The East Coast of India lies between the Eastern Ghats mountain range and the Bay of Bengal. This region is relatively flat and fertile, making it suitable for agriculture and home to several major cities and important ports along the coast. The West Coast of India lies between the Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin, along the Arabian Sea, and includes the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Kerala. Karnataka is located between Maharashtra and Kerala, while the state of Gujarat and the Union Territory of Daman and Diu lie between Diu and Kerala.

questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Punjab.Key Points

  • The Peninsular Plateau in India is a large region of elevated land that lies to the south of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
  • It is mainly composed of Precambrian rocks that are millions of years old.
  • The plateau covers parts of several Indian states, including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala.
  • However, Punjab is not a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
  • It is located in the northwest of India and is mainly composed of alluvial plains and river valleys.

Additional Information

  • The Peninsular Plateau is characterized by its composition of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
  • Maharashtra is a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the Deccan Plateau, which is a large volcanic plateau that covers much of central and southern India.
  • Madhya Pradesh is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges, as well as parts of the Deccan Plateau.
  • Tamil Nadu is a state in the south of India that is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
  • It includes the Eastern Ghats mountain range and the Nilgiri Hills.
